cur:manuscripts-girona-beatus-sixth-seal.summary: In a red medallion inscribed 'Thronus Dei', Christ with a cross-nimbus sits enthroned, holding a book and stretching out his hand, between six-winged cherubim and seraphim, while the four living creatures and elders stand below. In the lower registers the sun is darkened, the moon turns to blood, stars fall, and people hide among the mountains from 'the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb'.
facts: With 184 surviving miniatures on 284 leaves, it is described as one of the most richly decorated and best documented of the Beatus commentaries.

The Girona Beatus was completed on 6 July 975 for an abbot Dominicus, probably at the monastery of Tábara; unusually, its painters are named: 'Ende, woman painter and servant of God', and the monk-priest Emeterius.

getty:12a91807-8e45-4fa1-b6aa-f5979a6072.summary: A bronze bowl-shaped censer still hangs from a length of its twisted chain. Around its body are round medallions with busts in relief; the one turned to the front shows Christ with a cross-marked halo, between stylised plant ornaments. As incense smoke rose from it during the liturgy, the faces of Christ, the Virgin and the apostles circled the worshippers.
facts: The Getty describes four medallions: Christ, Saint Peter, the Virgin Mary and probably Saint Paul.
Three suspension loops survive, one only partly, with four and a half links of one length of twisted S-shaped chain; the censer is 10 cm high.
It was given to the Getty in 1979 by Lee Rizzuto.

walters:W.185.225V.summary: God the Father, bearded and crowned with a golden nimbus, sits on a Gothic throne before a gold-and-blue lozenge ground and holds out the cross on which the crucified Christ hangs. This 'Throne of Grace' image presents the Father offering the Son's sacrifice to the viewer. Framed by delicate gold-leaf sprays, it opens the Hours of the Eternal Wisdom in this Utrecht Book of Hours.
facts: The miniature introduces Matins of the Hours of the Eternal Wisdom (fol. 225v), the only full-page miniature in that section of the book.
The Doffinnes Hours contains both Latin and Dutch texts; its calendar is for the Use of Utrecht, which localises its production there.
The original owners, probably a married couple, were once painted kneeling beside the Crucifixion miniature (fol. 72v) but were later erased and overpainted.
walters:W.185.225V.notes: Worklist year 750 was a parsing error. The dove of the Holy Spirit is not clearly visible at this image size.

Q75192045.summary: Christ has fallen beneath the cross in the middle of a vast, crowded procession winding up toward Calvary, surrounded by soldiers, trumpeters, horsemen and grieving followers. Tiepolo turns the Passion into a sweeping theatrical pageant, yet keeps the exhausted Christ as its still, sorrowing centre.
facts: It forms a Passion cycle in Sant'Alvise together with two smaller canvases by Tiepolo, the Crowning with Thorns and the Flagellation.
Tiepolo was the most sought-after decorative painter in 18th-century Europe, later working in Würzburg and at the royal palace in Madrid.
The painting remains in the Venetian church for which it was made.
